text: {"score":2,"justification":"Numbers match the card, but the framing and next steps contradict the evidence. The headline and leaning (high-acuity panel, 'Healthy-patient 99215 near peers') are not supported: the provider's 99215 share is 3.75x expected, risk-adjusted score 4.17, z=2.18, and 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in nearly every complexity stratum (e.g., 15.9% vs 4.1% at 1 condition, 22.5% vs 8.0% at 3). The next step states 'the documentation returned supports the level billed', yet zero records were returned, so this is fabricated and also conflicts with the summary's own 'Records came back for 0 claims' and 'No records requested'. The cited claims are two high-complexity examples that only support a benign story; the low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0099148 with 0 conditions, C0099067 an 18-year-old with diabetes) that would be most useful are not cited. 'Mild elevation on 1-condition visits' understates a ~4x ratio. The summary does not recommend requesting documentation, the obvious action.","problems":["Next step claims documentation supports the billed level, but no documentation was returned (0 documented claims) — unsupported and contradictory","Headline 'near peers' and leaning 'high acuity panel' contradict z=2.18, ratio 3.75x, and excess ~25.7 99215 claims","'Mild elevation' on 1-condition visits misdescribes 15.9% vs 4.1% all-provider share","Cited examples are only high-complexity claims; low-complexity 99215 claims not cited","No recommendation to request records for the cited or low-complexity visits; the 'No records requested' note conflicts with the lack of a next step to request","Does not clearly flag that missing documentation prevents any conclusion about support"]}
